in_sanskrit.name: अरुणा
in_sanskrit.long_meaning: The goddess of dawn, the personification of the red color, or the one who appears before the sun. In Hindu mythology, Aruna is depicted as the charioteer of the sun god Surya, riding on a chariot pulled by seven horses.

in_hindi.name: अरुणा
in_hindi.long_meaning: Aruna in Hindi has an alternative meaning 'second', as it is the second wife of King Yayati in Hindu mythology.

in_tamil.name: அருணா
in_tamil.long_meaning: Aruna in Tamil is considered a synonym for 'Atmavijayam', meaning 'victory of the self' or 'self-realization'.

in_telugu.name: అరుణ
in_telugu.long_meaning: Aruna in Telugu is also known as 'Adyudu', meaning 'first' or 'original', which can be interpreted as the first light of dawn or the original form of the goddess.

in_marathi.name: Aruna
in_marathi.meaning: हिंदू नाव म्हणजे Goddess of Dawn
in_marathi.long_meaning: Aruna हे एक हिंदू नाव आहे जे भारतीय संस्कृतीत खोल आध्यात्मिक महत्त्व ठेवते। Aruna is the goddess of dawn in Hindu mythology. She is also known as the charioteer of the sun god Surya. Her name is derived from the Sanskrit word 'arun' which means red, symbolizing the color of the dawn sky.

in_bengali.name: Aruna
in_bengali.meaning: হিন্দু নাম যার অর্থ Goddess of Dawn
in_bengali.long_meaning: Aruna একটি হিন্দু নাম যা ভারতীয় সংস্কৃতিতে গভীর আধ্যাত্মিক তাৎপর্য রাখে। Aruna is the goddess of dawn in Hindu mythology. She is also known as the charioteer of the sun god Surya. Her name is derived from the Sanskrit word 'arun' which means red, symbolizing the color of the dawn sky.
